principles: Single source: enrich the one renderer so all 3 surfaces auto-inherit and stay byte-identical.
Backward-compat: keep the existing refresh_stale+validate lines and the EVIDENCE_STALE_MARKER constant.
Projection not new logic: the drift-class line reflects existing storyFilesHash-secondary behavior, not a new rule.
drivers: A Host reading the stale hint cannot tell unrelated-drift (refresh) from story-owned drift (re-review).
Put the guidance at the moment of the hint, complementing the B-5396 runbook.

options.name: enrich the shared renderer
pros: Single source: all 3 surfaces auto-inherit; byte-identity preserved
~2 lines in one core file + 1 smoke update; low-risk (not a high-risk lifecycle path)
Puts the guidance at the moment the Host reads the stale hint
cons: Must update the one byte-equality smoke (extractStaleBlock slice)

options.name: rewrite the DONE-blocker generators (machine.ts/done-oracle.ts)
pros: Guidance at the DONE gate too
cons: The spike refuted this: DONE gate already suggests done_prepare; the gap is the earlier hint

options.name: add a separate new hint alongside the shared one
pros: No change to the existing renderer
cons: Breaks the single-source byte-identity invariant (B-a2f1); two hints to keep in sync

rationale: The spike validated this is a ~2-line change in one core file (single source -> 3 surfaces auto-inherit) plus one byte-equality smoke update, with no high-risk lifecycle exposure. Option B (rewrite DONE-blocker generators) was refuted by the spike (gate already suggests done_prepare; high-risk 3x2). Option C breaks the single-source byte-identity invariant.

preMortem.mitigation: Update the byte-equality asserts + the extractStaleBlock line-count slice in the same change; run the smoke green before REVIEW.

preMortem.mitigation: Frame the drift-class line as the current storyFilesHash-secondary behavior (B-6de6/B-d243), worded as guidance not a guarantee; it mirrors the just-merged runbook wording.

preMortem.consequence: That surface would not inherit the new lines -> byte divergence.
